title: Bench time
text: A teammate is angry about being benched and asks you to skip practice together.
choices: Ask the coach for a development plan
ends: The coach sets training goals; your teammate has a route back.
Both absences are recorded. Loyalty has cost the team preparation.
Your teammate keeps attending and gains a practice partner.

title: Who made the play?
text: The group praises your winning shot, overlooking the classmate who created the opening.
choices: Credit the pass in front of everyone
ends: The teammate notices the omission and trusts you less.
The whole play gets recognised, including the assist.
Your teammate appreciates it, although the public story stays incomplete.

title: Exam notes
text: Your study group finds an answer sheet that may belong to tomorrow's test.
choices: Ask the teacher for a fair practice set
ends: The group learns the methods; the leaked answers stay unused.
Your classmates now know you will share compromised work.
The teacher replaces the practice material and keeps the assessment fair.

title: Too fast
text: A classmate stops asking questions because the study group rushes past every explanation.
choices: Explain one example at their pace
ends: The classmate withdraws; speed has replaced support.
They solve the next example themselves after patient practice.
A smaller group makes it easier for them to ask questions.

title: The group photo
text: Someone wants to post an unflattering photo of a classmate for laughs.
ends: The classmate declines, and the group respects their answer.
The post gets attention at the cost of the classmate's trust.
The picture stays off the feed; nobody becomes the joke.

title: The guest list
text: A friend suggests an expensive party that would leave several classmates unable to join.
choices: Keep the party and add a free meetup
ends: The price becomes a test of belonging; some classmates stay away.
The group meets without making money an entry requirement.
There are two chances to meet, though the expensive party still divides attendance.

title: A borrowed look
text: A classmate copies your friend's handmade jacket and calls it their own idea.
choices: Explain the work and ask for credit
Offer to help make their own design
ends: The argument gets louder while the original work remains uncredited.
Your friend's design gets its credit without a public pile-on.
A new design takes shape; your friend appreciates the care over copying.

title: More than a label
text: A newcomer likes the music but worries that the group expects them to change their whole appearance.
choices: Let them try one meetup first
ends: The newcomer shares music without needing to become a copy of anyone.
The group becomes another place where belonging requires a costume.
They try the meetup with room to decide whether it suits them.

title: The understudy
text: The lead loses their voice. Your friend wants to perform anyway rather than let the understudy go on.
choices: Support the understudy and the resting lead
ends: The pressure makes your friend feel expendable when they are unwell.
The understudy gets their chance and the lead keeps a place in the production.
The smaller performance protects the lead but gives the understudy less stage time.

title: A harsh review
text: A rough audience comment reaches your friend just before rehearsal.
choices: Read the comment aloud for laughs
ends: Your friend has one useful improvement to rehearse.
They feel reassured, but the weak scene stays unaddressed.
The rehearsal becomes humiliating; your friend remembers who made it worse.

title: A locked spot
text: The usual skating area is closed for repairs. Someone suggests jumping the barrier.
ends: The group gets a session without entering the repair area.
The outing ends at the restricted area; your friend questions your judgement.
The boards are ready for next time, even without today's skating session.

title: The fall clip
text: A classmate's fall is the funniest part of a skating video, but they ask you to cut it.
choices: Remove it and use an agreed clip
Ask them to choose the edit
ends: The views rise while your classmate's willingness to film with you falls.
The video uses an agreed clip and your classmate returns for the next session.
They choose a version they can laugh at too, with control over how they appear.

title: Too loud
text: One player's louder sound is drowning out your friend's part during a jam.
ends: Every part can be heard, and the group finishes a coherent arrangement.
The volume contest buries the arrangement and strains the group.
Each player gets a clear lead while the rest practise supporting them.

title: A missing player
text: Your friend cannot make the weekend rehearsal because of family duties.
choices: Send a recording and agree another slot
Rehearse only the parts you can
ends: Your friend finds out they were replaced and stops relying on the group.
They practise from the recording and return knowing the revised plan.
The session stays useful, though the full arrangement waits until everyone is there.

title: The new teammate
text: Your friend keeps losing matches while learning a new role, and the group wants to drop them.
choices: Offer a role they already know
ends: The friend learns without every mistake costing the ranked team.
The friend loses their place and knows the group would not help them learn.
The team stabilises, though learning the new role has to wait.

title: One more match
text: A late tournament round would leave your friend exhausted for tomorrow's school assessment.
choices: Leave on time and find a substitute
ends: The group stays late; your friend remembers the pressure when they needed rest.
The tournament carries on without asking everyone to sacrifice tomorrow.
The friend keeps their study time, and the next meetup stays on the calendar.

title: A shared wall
text: Two friends want the same space in a small student exhibition.
choices: Agree a rotation and credit both
ends: The display rewards status rather than the work, and your friend notices.
Both artists get an agreed display slot with their names attached.
The joint piece fits, though both artists have to compromise on scale.

title: The last paints
text: The group has enough donated paint for one shared piece or several tiny individual studies.
choices: Agree a shared plan before using it
Keep the best colours for yourself
ends: The group finishes one piece with agreed roles and credit.
Your studies use the best supplies while others cannot finish theirs.
Everyone gets a small study, though the group gives up the larger piece.

title: The reading choice
text: A friend wants the group to read a long book that several members cannot finish.
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: The cleanup route
text: A classmate points out that the planned cleanup route is inaccessible.
choices: Give everyone a choice of roles
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: A borrowed tool
text: Your friend's tool comes back damaged after a group project.
choices: Own the damage and arrange repair
Ask the group to help replace it
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: The lunch corner
text: A classmate enjoys the group but needs quieter lunch breaks.
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: A joke too far
text: A joke about a classmate gets laughs but clearly upsets them.
choices: Change the joke to something harmless
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: The trail plan
text: Your friend worries the proposed trail is too difficult for the group.
choices: Choose a route everyone can manage
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: The outfit price
text: The group suggests a matching outfit that your friend cannot afford.
choices: Build looks from what everyone owns
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: The petition
text: A classmate wants to sign but disagrees with one demand.
choices: Let them support a narrower request
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.

title: A missed deadline
text: Your friend is struggling to keep up with the group's study timetable.
choices: Study together for one short session
ends: Your friend remembers the practical support and stays involved.
The pressure damages your friend's trust in the group.
The compromise gives your friend a way to take part.
